GitHub repository: drogers0/aistat — 14 GitHub/Stars, checked 2026/10/16 Fri.
A Go command-line tool that reports Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot usage limits from their existing credential stores; it can also switch stored Claude and Codex accounts.
Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows through Git Bash or WSL.
Review required before installation or use; the small adoption footprint makes independent inspection especially important.

The installer downloads a release archive and checksum file from the same GitHub release, verifies the SHA-256 checksum, then removes macOS quarantine from the installed binary. Verify the release and installation path independently before running it.

The CLI reads provider credentials and sends authenticated requests to provider usage endpoints. Its account-switch command can rewrite the active Claude or Codex credential shared by other sessions on the device; review token handling and credential writes before using that command.
Review sources: installer, README and authentication behavior.

Aletheia is the Greek word Heidegger uses for truth understood as unconcealment: something comes out of hiddenness and becomes manifest.
Person/Martin Heidegger develops this sense of truth in Person/Martin Heidegger/Essay/35/The Origin of the Work of Art, where a work of art can open a world and let beings appear.
In GitP/Light, aletheia names the character of a listening moment in which a sound reveals something about a Microfreak/Preset.
Related terms: unconcealment describes the appearing; insight names the recognition that can come with it.
When a list of entities is sorted in the order of the alphabet, that's called alphabetical order

When speaking of OS/File/Systems or other programs that sort things such as Spreadsheets, then, to refer to the order in which files are sorted, one should instead use the term Lexicographic/Order or say that files are sorted Lexicographically, which applies an order to all the characters that are valid names that are not parts of the alphabet

A general-purpose mechanical computer designed by Person/Charles Babbage, first described in 18/3/7. It was never built.
The mill did arithmetic and the store held numbers, the same split later computers make between processor and memory.
Programs and data went in on punched cards, borrowed from the Jacquard loom that wove patterns into cloth.
The design allowed loops and conditional branching, which is what makes it general-purpose rather than a calculator.
It followed Babbage's Difference Engine, which could only compute tables of polynomial values.

Person/Ada Lovelace's 1843 notes describe what it could do, including a program for Bernoulli numbers. She wrote that it "weaves algebraical patterns just as the Jacquard-loom weaves flowers and leaves."
Babbage's son Henry built part of the mill around 1910. No complete engine has been built.

Cultural anthropology studies how people make meaning and organize social life across communities and historical settings. It examines practices, institutions, values, relationships, and the ways people describe their own worlds.

The American Anthropological Association describes cultural anthropology as one of the discipline's four fields and emphasizes the study of how people use language, make meaning, and organize social action.

Cultural anthropologists observe communities in context and attend to the accounts people give of their own practices. Methods vary by question and community; no single method represents the whole field.

Cultural explanations are strongest when they attend to differences within a community as well as differences between communities. Culture is learned and contested, not a fixed trait shared identically by every member of a group.
